title: sign.rs: boundary derived from SHA-256 of content is correct — prevents collision and ensures test reproducibility
description: boundary_from_content() uses the first 16 bytes of SHA-256(content) as the MIME boundary. This is correct for two reasons: (1) it satisfies RFC 2046 §5.1.1 which requires the boundary to not appear in the body, and the code explicitly checks for this; (2) it is deterministic, making test output reproducible. A future contributor might simplify this to a random UUID or a fixed string. Random UUIDs require getrandom and break snapshot tests. A fixed string would collide with any content that contains that literal. The SHA-256 derivation is the right balance.
